one_month_reasoning: The window ends 2026-11-01, a Sunday, so the effective mark is the 2026-10-30 close. Lumentum has not announced its Q1 FY27 date. Past fiscal Q1 prints came on Nov 2 2023, Nov 7 2024 and Nov 4 2025 (supervisor's EDGAR check), so the print is expected around Nov 3-6 and is very likely outside the window; in round 1 I relied on a third-party Nov 3 date. Inside the window: late-October hyperscaler earnings and 2027 capex guides (Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon), which can move AI optics by 10%+ either way; peer prints that may land just inside or outside (Coherent ~Nov 4, AAOI early Nov per StockAnalysis); the company's date announcement (usually mid-October, not market-moving); and continuing 10b5-1 insider sales. The insider sales are confirmed (CFO 24,542 shares at $1,048.50 on 10/1) but are a modest supply overhang, not a signal. After a +18% week to a 52-week high, short-horizon reversal and momentum roughly cancel. I use a lognormal with median about $1,078 (a hair below spot) and about 26% monthly vol (97%/3.5 = 27.7%, slightly shrunk), so P(>= spot) = 0.49, close to neutral.

fair_value.method: Blend at the Oct-2027 horizon: P/E (NTM-at-horizon EPS $34 x 30x + $10.7 net cash = $1031, weight 0.5), forward EV/EBITDA at the peer median 23.1x (NTM EBITDA ~$4.47B, giving $1013/sh, weight 0.3), and a cycle-normalised P/E where the haircut sits on EPS only (mid-cycle EPS $26 x 30x + net cash = $791, weight 0.2), on 103M diluted shares. Result about $975, about 10% below spot.

bear.story: AI-capex digestion plus supply catch-up. Chinese 200G EML (Changguang Huaxin from Q4 2026; Yuanjie and others after customer verification) and Coherent/Broadcom capacity close the gap during 2027. EML pricing resets, Customer A (26.6% of revenue) digests inventory, and CPO slips. NTM EPS ~$24 x ~21x (bottom-third of the peer range) + net cash, about $520.

base.story: Execution continues. FY27 lands near the $20-22 consensus and FY28 near $33. By Oct-2027 the market pays about 30x (around the peer median) on ~$34 NTM EPS as growth slows from 110% to about 50% and then lower: about $1,030, roughly flat from $1,085.

bull.story: The InP shortage lasts into 2028 (C114 cites the substrate deficit to 2028). CPO/ELS orders pull forward, OFC-2027 targets are raised, and EPS heads toward the CEO's ~$40 earnings power, with NTM ~$42 x ~41x (upper part of the peer range, e.g. Astera at 60x), about $1,750.

thesis_break_reason: Around $660 (-39%): that is 20x FY28 consensus EPS ($33) plus net cash, a multiple in the bottom third of the 12-peer range, about where only the Chinese module makers and Broadcom trade, and below the spring-2026 pullback lows. Getting there would most likely require FY28 earnings power itself to be cut (an EML pricing reset from Chinese InP capacity, a Customer A order cut, or a hyperscaler capex cut). Peer-wide multiple compression alone would most likely stop above that.

reasoning: Round 2 changes. (1) EPS base: the supervisor showed my round-1 Street range was a stale cluster of recaps. Current consensus is FY27 ~$19.8-21.8 and FY28 ~$33.0-34.7 (MarketBeat via supervisor; StockAnalysis 2026-10-03). I move FY28 to $33 (low end) and NTM-at-horizon to $34. (2) My round-1 EV/sales leg used FY28 revenue of $7.5B, well below the $9.68B consensus. Combined with $32 EPS it implied an impossible 44% net margin, so I replaced it with a forward EV/EBITDA leg at the peer median. (3) Following the supervisor, the cycle-normalised leg now haircuts EPS only ($26), not EPS and multiple both. (4) Comps: across 12 AI-optics and connectivity peers, the median NTM P/E is 31.9x and the median forward EV/EBITDA is 23.1x. LITE's next-year revenue growth is in line with the peer median, so I give no premium. 30x sits just under the median and inside the range. (5) Skeptic follow-ups: the Yuanjie claim was overstated. Reputable sources say Yuanjie is still in customer verification, but Changguang Huaxin (China Daily, 2026-07-24) plans 200G EML production in Q4 2026 for large 2027 deliveries. C114 (2026-09-02) says the InP substrate deficit could last to 2028, which cuts against the bear case on timing. The Dec-2026 convert maturity is immaterial ($54.8M), and the insider selling is confirmed but pre-planned. The result: fair value of about $975 (up from $900, still ~10% below spot and below the supervisor's ~$1,050, because I keep a 20% weight on a normalised-EPS leg and a sub-median multiple for concentration risk). Scenarios of $520/$1,030/$1,750 at 25/50/25 give a mean of ~$1,080 and a median of ~$1,030. The ladder is a lognormal with median ~$1,025 and sigma ~0.66 (below the 97% realized vol, part of which was a one-off re-rating), with a slightly fattened left tail, so P(>= $1,085) = 0.47. Research was limited: Alpha Vantage was rate-limited and Twelve Data statistics need a paid plan, so peer multiples come from StockAnalysis pages (S&P Global data). Forward EV/EBITDA is my own build from consensus EPS, not a quoted figure.

comps_summary.peer_median_revenue_growth_next_fy: +53% (12-peer median of consensus next-fiscal-year revenue growth); LITE +52.8% (FY28)
comps_summary.lite_today: NTM P/E 43.4x (price $1,085.42 / NTM EPS $25.02); forward EV/EBITDA 33.6x (EV $110.7B on 103M diluted shares / NTM EBITDA $3.3B). Sources: StockAnalysis LITE statistics and forecast, 2026-10-03.
comps_summary.lite_in_my_methods: P/E leg 30x (about 6% below the 31.9x median, inside the 12.5-60.4x range); EV/EBITDA leg 23.1x (at the median, inside the 10.4-49.8x range); normalised leg 30x on haircut EPS.
comps_summary.method: All peer numbers come from StockAnalysis (S&P Global Market Intelligence data), statistics and forecast pages fetched 2026-10-03. Forward P/E = price / NTM consensus EPS (this-FY and next-FY consensus time-weighted to Oct-2026 to Sep-2027 by each company's fiscal year end). Forward EV/EBITDA = EV / (NTM EPS x shares / 0.85 + TTM D&A); this approximates non-GAAP EBITDA, ignores net interest, and treats all peers the same way. The Chinese peers are in CNY, so their multiples are currency-neutral. Corning was considered and dropped (diversified glass/display); the 12 shown are the most direct listed AI-optics and connectivity comparables. Lumentum has no other listed pure-play EML peer.
comps_summary.justification: I give no persistent premium, and a small discount on P/E. Growth: LITE's consensus next-year revenue growth (+52.8%) equals the peer median (+53%), and the Chinese transceiver leaders are growing faster (InnoLight +99%) at 12-14x, so growth cannot justify a premium. Margins and returns: LITE's ~40% non-GAAP operating-margin guide is well above Coherent (12.7% TTM GAAP), Fabrinet (10%) and Ciena (14%), similar to the Chinese module makers (39-44%), and below Broadcom (49%). But the gain from 15% to 40% came within a year on EML/pump-laser scarcity. China Daily (2026-07-24) shows a new 200G EML entrant producing from Q4 2026, and C114 (2026-09-02) shows the InP deficit could ease by 2028. That is evidence the margin edge is not yet proven persistent through the horizon, so I don't capitalise it with a premium multiple. Cyclicality: as a component maker with 42% of revenue from two customers (10-K), LITE is more cyclical than diversified Broadcom, Marvell or Corning, which argues for a discount. Balance sheet: ~$1.1B net cash is a plus versus levered Coherent, Ciena and Broadcom, but it is only ~1% of EV, so it does not move the multiple. Net: 30x P/E (just under the 31.9x median) and the median 23.1x EV/EBITDA, both inside the peer range. LITE's current 43x/34x sits in the upper quartile, which is the core of my skeptic view that the stock is priced above the peer-justified value.
